title: 'Quiet Questing' — Americans Want Switched Off Travel
paragraphs: Life comes with a lot of responsibilities. There's work to do, decisions to make, meals to plan and problems to solve.
So when it's finally time for a vacation, many people hope to switch off for a while.
But that doesn't always happen. And a new Talker Research survey of 2,000 Americans found that 51% always or often come home from a trip feeling completely drained.
One reason may be that some everyday responsibilities follow people on vacation.
When asked what they would most like a break from on vacation, 30% said cleaning, 28% said cooking and 27% said making sure everyone else is happy.
And many are already planning for 2027. On average, travelers have already planned two of the three trips they hope to take next year.
So what kinds of trips are Americans interested in?
Thirty-one percent said they would like to try "quiet questing" in 2027. That includes trips focused on peace and quiet, such as phone-free vacations and getting away from crowds.
Three in 10 also said they would like to travel "like a local," or to learn more about local life and traditions where they're traveling, instead of only visiting the best-known attractions.

Another 22% are interested in "selective splurging," meaning they wouldn't mind spending more than usual on things like food, accommodation or beauty treatments to make a vacation feel a little more special than everyday life.
And nearly one in five would even try something called "vacation ghosting" — taking a trip without telling friends or family until after they return, or not telling them at all.
So, whether it's switching off phones, spending a little extra, or keeping the whole trip secret, there's one thing US travelers are looking for in 2027: a real break!
